page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 48 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv8 arm64 architecture using the Neoverse-N1 model running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals strong multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core scoring in the top 25% at 72814.16. However, single-core performance is more modest, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is stable, registering 167.25 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations. Large-model LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with text generation on a 70B model scoring in the bottom 25% at 2.78 tokens/sec, and prompt processing on a 70B model falling into the bottom 10%.

The instance provides a high baseline network bandwidth of 75 Gbps, making it highly efficient for network-bound and EBS-optimized workloads. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the custom ARM64 architecture offers a high physical core density without hyperthreading, reducing resource contention for parallel processing. This profile is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, software compilation, and distributed database operations, whereas single-threaded tasks and large-scale AI inference represent clear performance tradeoffs.
